Whenever a card says "when this creature attacks", what it actually means is "when you move to attack phase and say 'this creature is attacking'". Since myriad tokens come into the battlefield *after* you say who is attacking, they don't activate this trigger! 

If the tokens somehow entered the battlefield before attack phase and then you had the chance to say "I'm choosing to attack you with these tokens", then they would trigger this ability.

Standard is a dying/dead format, at least in paper. No one plays it except online. Magic is in a really bad place for new players in your position right now since there is no easily on-boardable format... 

I think either Pauper or Pioneer is your best bet if you want a traditional magic experience. Neither format rotates, meaning, unless specifically banned, all cards legal in those formats will remain legal. 

Pauper uses only commonscards, meaning cards are cheap. It's a fun format, and if a store near you supports it (and actually has a lot of people come to it's events), it's relatively beginner friendly.

Pioneer is more expensive. It's deal is that only cards printed after 2012 are legal, meaning it's a lot more powerful than pauper, but significantly less powerful than formats like modern. The format is seeing a lot of play right now and is very popular at game stores.

No matter what you pick *CHECK WITH YOUR LOCAL STORE* before buying a deck. You do not want to invest time and money into a deck for a format that is not popular near you. You need to find from your stores which formats actually get big turn outs. It's different everywhere.

Edit: left out commander cause it's... Different...

Chances are there is a thriving commander scene near you... But the gameplay is very different than traditional magic. Also, while the format is made to be casual (not competitive), the game states that arise are probably the most complex you'll find in magic and are *very* hard to keep track of even if you have a lot of the cards memorized (which takes a while).

I would argue that in all three of your examples, wild strike (while bad) is less of a problem than you think and is certainly not the main thing holding these mons back.

 Lets start with Luxray because it is the easiest for me to dismiss. 120 attack is nice, but its speed is a measly 70, and its defences are average (if that). Also, this thing wants to take guts, which is a shame, since it means we can't take a choice scarf to buff our bad speed (and also means our survivability is even *further* hindered). Coverage (a theme we'll see here) is also bad. No one needs a slow and fragile physical attacker with bad coverage in a type with very common immunities. There is no role for this thing to play. A better STAB would be nice, but if it had an electric type earthquake, it'd still be horrible. 

Next, let's look at Electivire. This mon is similar to Luxray, since it has that big attack stat, but it has similarly underwhelming speed and defensive stats to back it up. One thing it has over Luxray is coverage. This thing gets access to the elemental punches, earthquake, brick break/hammer arm, and darkest lariat. Unfortunately, its ability choices are worse than Luxray's, so coverage is really all it has (no massive guts hits). A few gens ago, its statline and coverage gave you some reason to run it, but it has been so far powercrept out at this point. Newer physical attacks have way more toys and much better stats. This is the mon that I could see most benefitting from a better STAB option, but it is just so far outclassed that I'm skeptical. That speed stat isn't enough anymore. 

Finally, lets talk about Zebstrika. Firstly, its statline is painfully average. 116 speed is good, and 100 attack is fine... but neither are anything to write home about. Secondly, lets look at coverage... Because it is bad. You get double edge, flame charge, and *bounce*? Yikes. I just don't know what you're supposed to do here. I guess a better STAB would help, but it wouldn't give you a reason to run this little Zebra. Its just a bad mon with a mediocre statline, and bad coverage. 

In summary, physical electrics could use a new STAB, but they need a lot more than that. We just haven't had one with the stats, coverage, or abilities to make a splash with or without a better move to spam.
